$comment: Generic device catalog: devices, displays, postures, folds and platform profiles. Sizes are in the unit of the device platform (pt on iOS, dp on Android). App-specific screens and layout rules live in a profile.

sources.figma-tokens: Design tokens: device and orientation safe-area insets (hSafeAreaInset 24/62, bottomSafeAreaInset 21)
sources.apple-device: Apple device spec (not in our Figma: Figma frames are 375×812 portrait / 812 landscape)
sources.estimated: Estimated: not confirmed. Verify in Xcode 27.1 Device Hub.
sources.material3: Material 3 adaptive guidance and component specs: m3.material.io/foundations/layout/applying-layout
sources.device-spec: Manufacturer device specification (pixels and default density); dp derived as px / density
sources.observed: Observed on hardware or an emulator while testing an Android app
sources.microsoft-learn: Microsoft Learn, Surface Duo screen dimensions: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/dual-screen/android/surface-duo-dimensions
sources.android-studio-avd: Android Studio device definitions (AOSP sdklib devices/nexus.xml)
sources.apple-hig: Apple Human Interface Guidelines, Layout (developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) and UIKit system layout margins

sizeClasses.$comment: Real devices use the explicit table under each display. Free resize has no device, so it uses these thresholds.

verticalBars.$comment: Geometry of the trailing-edge rail on iPhone Duo (HIG: Dynamic Island, status bar, toolbar, tab bar from top to bottom). All estimated until confirmed in Xcode 27.1 Device Hub.

fold.$comment: How layouts adapt when a display is partially folded (HIG › Adapt your layout when the device folds).
fold.$balanceMargins: Match the display symmetry: equal leading/trailing margins so content centres on the fold.
fold.$evenGridGutterAtFold: Grids with an even number of columns put their middle gutter over the fold (fold width + gap).

fontScale.$note: Dynamic Type does not scale every style by one factor; a linear multiplier approximates Larger Text.

sizeClasses.$comment: androidx.window.core.layout.WindowSizeClass breakpoints, computed from the window size in dp, never from the orientation.
sizeClasses.$note: Large (1200) and Extra-large (1600) come from androidx.window 1.5 (BREAKPOINTS_V2). The brief names 1200 as the desktop-class breakpoint; both are modelled.

navigation.$comment: Which navigation pattern a window gets, first match wins. Mirrors NavigationSuiteScaffold, plus the drawer on large windows as the sample app's decision.

rules.$note: NavigationSuiteScaffold keeps a bottom bar in tabletop posture.
A short window keeps its height for content: bars move to the leading edge.
NavigationSuiteScaffold does not pick a drawer by default; the sample app uses a permanent drawer on desktop-class windows. Confirm with design.

bar.$note: The sample app draws its tab bar as a floating pill over the content. M3 NavigationBar is 80 dp and docked.

fold.$comment: How layouts adapt to a FoldingFeature (Material 3 › Foldables; androidx.window). Split only when isSeparating is true, and split at the hinge bounds, not at 50%.
fold.$avoidOcclusion: When occlusionType is FULL the hinge hides content: nothing interactive may sit in its bounds.

nonLinear.$comment: Android 14+ FontScaleConverter: sp in, dp out. Large text grows less than small text. Between tables the platform interpolates.
nonLinear.$note: Tables from AOSP FontScaleConverterFactory. Verify against the Android version you test on.

split.$note: Split-screen divider thickness and snap ratios vary by OEM.

freeform.$note: Desktop windowing draws a caption bar the app gets as WindowInsets.Type.captionBar().

popup.$note: Samsung pop-up view: a small floating window with a handle bar.

displaySize.$note: Settings › Display size scales the density. The steps differ per device; these are typical.

notes.title: targetSdk 36 ignores orientation and resizability on large screens
notes.text: From Android 16, apps targeting API 36 no longer get screenOrientation, resizeableActivity, minAspectRatio or maxAspectRatio honoured on displays whose smallest width is 600 dp or more. The app is resized whether it opts in or not.

notes.title: Split on isSeparating, not on the fold state
notes.text: A FLAT crease on a flexible display does not separate anything. Split the layout only when FoldingFeature.isSeparating is true, and split at the hinge bounds.

notes.title: Size classes come from the window
notes.text: Split-screen, desktop windowing and pop-up view resize the window without any hardware change. Read WindowSizeClass from the current window metrics, never from the device or the orientation.

layoutDefaults.$comment: Page layout per size class when no app profile says otherwise. Values follow Material 3's layout guidance (margins 16/24 dp, one pane below expanded) and the earlier Material column grid; iOS follows UIKit's system margins.
